header.flow: Workflow: {data} → {train} → {match}. Jobs run one at a time in background processes; closing this page or the UI does not stop them. Use the Dashboard ({url}) for simulations, results and replays.
side.lost: Lost: the process is alive but silent; the queue is paused
missing.error: This Python is missing packages the ML UI needs: {names}
missing.python: Python used by the ML UI right now: `{python}`
missing.fix: Run the line below in a terminal (it names this exact Python so the packages land in the right place), then close the ML UI and start it again:
missing.note: With several Pythons installed (for example Anaconda and python.org) a bare `pip install` can install into another one.
job.lost_help: Lost: the process is still running but has not reported progress for 30 seconds. Queued jobs wait for it to finish or report again; press "Force end" only when you are sure it is stuck (it ends the job and the Runner it started).
progress.publish: Publishing the Runner (the C# sources are newer than the published build)…
remark.full_log: Full log: pick this job under “Job details” below.
remark.interrupted: Process is gone (computer slept, shut down or was killed)
remark.lost: Process alive but silent; queue paused
remark.match: Win rate {win} ± {ci} ({games} games), recorded on the model
queue.card_sub: One at a time, in the order added; the queue keeps going if you close the ML UI, and after a failed or cancelled job. Shows the latest 40 finished jobs.
queue.col.name: Name
queue.details: Job details (log, validation loss curve, result)
copy.label: Copy summary for AI
copy.fail: Copy failed (the browser blocked the clipboard)
detail.gone: This job's record no longer exists.
detail.waiting: Waiting (No. {n} in the queue); starts automatically when the jobs ahead finish
detail.cancel_note: Cancelling data generation keeps the games already finished (except on Windows); cancelling training leaves no model; a cancelled match is not recorded on the model. The next queued job then starts.
detail.interrupted: The process is gone (computer slept, shut down or was killed).
detail.model_saved: Model saved to `{path}`. Next, go to “{match}” and play it against the original MCTS: win rate is the real criterion.
detail.dump_result: {status}: {games} games, {rows} rows → `{path}`. You can select it on the “{train}” page.
detail.match_done: Win rate {win} ± {ci} ({games} games), recorded in the model's `.meta.json`. The result file `{path}` can also be opened in the Dashboard.
detail.copy_note: Copies this job's settings, numbers, duration and versions to paste into a conversation with an AI. No per-game data; paths are relative to the project root.
ver.stale: The version list (docs/versions.json) disagrees with the version numbers in the code: {names}. Add what changed in this version.
ver.caption: The Dashboard's “Version Control” page shows the same list. The rules version covers only the game rules and randomness; each strategy has its own strategy version (at the bottom of this page); the engine version is for people; hashes use the rules, strategy, feature and data format versions to tell whether data and models are out of date.
ver.strategy_mismatch: The version list and the strategy versions in the code disagree: {names}.
act.queue_note: A job is running: this one will be No. {pos} in the queue, with {ahead} ahead of it; it keeps going in order even if you close the ML UI (also after a failed or cancelled job)
problem.reader: The queued or running job “{title}” reads this file, so it cannot be overwritten; choose another name
same.cannot_read: A {noun} with this name exists but its parameters cannot be read, so they cannot be compared.
same.identical: The {noun} with this name has **identical** parameters (hash {hash}): running again gives the same result, no need to overwrite.
same.differs:
The {noun} with this name has **different** parameters; overwriting replaces it:

{diff}
same.users: Models that used it: {names}. After overwriting, those models' records no longer match the data; choose another name.
match.table.default: Against the original MCTS (hand-written strategies at the table too)
match.table.hand: Against hand-written strategies (the table of analysis section 5)
match.table.model: Against another value model (hand-written strategies at the table too)
match.card: Match Validation: a model-based MCTS plays a set of games
match.intro: Plays a set of games with balanced seats to compare the win rate of the value-model MCTS; the result is recorded in the model's `.meta.json` and can also be opened in the Dashboard. Two comparisons matter: the same number of simulations (is the model more accurate?) and about the same time (is it worth it?): v2's inference cost leaves only about 180 simulations in the time of 300. To compare two models, choose “Against another value model” (two MCTS at one table); the result is recorded only on the model chosen above, the other model's records do not change.
match.only_one: There is only this one {n}-player model, nothing to play against.
match.games: Games (multiple of {perm} = every seat permutation equally often)
match.table_line: At the table: {seats}. Reference: about {lo}–{hi} minutes on 4 cores (depends on simulations).
match.name: Name (config ml/local/matches/<name>.json, result results/ml/<name>.json)
match.twins: This model already has a match with the same recipe: {list}. Running it again gives the same result.
match.p.name: The name cannot be empty or contain path characters or spaces
match.p.games: Games must be a multiple of {perm}
match.p.pending: A queued or running job already writes this result file; choose another name
match.note.model_changed: The model file was updated; this match was played by an older version
match.pick: Copy summary for AI: which match
match.pick_help: Copies the settings, win rates, duration and versions (no per-game data; paths are relative to the project root) to paste into a conversation with an AI.
mlist.card_sub: Every model in official ml/models/ and local ml/local/models/; for one model's details and management go to the “{page}” page.
mlist.col.best: Best win rate vs original MCTS
mlist.footer: Showing {shown} / {total} models. No quick filter selected = all. Location: git = official models (ml/models/, tracked by git), local = local models (ml/local/models/).
md.promote_text: Moves `{name}` (with its `.meta.json` and `.check.txt`) to `ml/models/`. Commit it afterwards in Visual Studio so it enters git and other computers and Claude can see it. Also add a row to the model list in `docs/models.md`.
md.local_note: Local model: only on this computer (ml/local/models/), not in git.
md.demoted: {name} was moved to the local workspace (ml/local/models/).
md.demote_note: This model is in the official folder ml/models/ but git does not track it (for example one trained in the ML UI earlier): moving it to local stops it from appearing in Visual Studio's Git changes.
md.rn.p.name: The name cannot be empty, and cannot contain path characters or spaces
md.rn.p.busy: The queued or running job “{title}” uses this model; wait until it finishes or remove it from the queue first
md.rn.caption: Renames `{name}`, `{name}.meta.json` and `{name}.check.txt` together (training and match records go with it). The hash does not include the name, so it does not change.
md.rn.refs:
Other models' records (match opponents, self-play data) are changed to the new name too:

{list}
md.rn.official: Records of official models (tracked by git) are not changed and keep the old name: {list}
md.rn.cfgs: Also change the value-model path in these config files (so that running them again still finds the model):
md.rn.stale:
These still point to this model by its old name: after renaming, **running them again will not find the model**, and the hash of self-play data made with it also changes because the model under the old name cannot be found. Data files keep the path from when they were made and are not changed.

{items}
md.no_meta: `{name}` has no `.meta.json` (how it was trained is unknown).
md.help.r2: How much of the “variation in outcomes” the model explains: 0 is as bad as always guessing the average, 1 is a perfect guess. Higher is better. Only comparable on the same validation data; judge a model by its match win rate.
md.help.ce: The loss that training actually lowers: the gap between the model's 0–1 return and the real result; confident wrong guesses are punished hard. Closer to 0 is better. Only comparable on the same validation data; judge a model by its match win rate.
md.no_best: No match against the original MCTS yet.
md.dash_note: Result files can be opened on the Dashboard ({url}) “Results” and “Compare” pages.
md.valid_note: Validation scores only check that training did not break; R² cannot be compared across different data distributions.
md.no_curve: No record (old model or backfilled meta).
md.no_feat: Only LightGBM has it (MLP and backfilled meta do not).
md.stale_warn: Some of this model's data was made with older rules or older strategies ({notes}): it learned positions under the old version; regenerate the data with the current version and retrain.
md.cmp.note: Blue bold = the best model in that row (highest win rate, R² and data rows; lowest cross-entropy); “Different” marks rows where parameters differ. Judge a model only by its match win rate.
md.none: No models yet (official ml/models/ and local ml/local/models/ are both empty).
md.pick_hint: Choose two or more models to compare parameters, data and win rates.
md.m.r2.meaning: How much of the “variation in outcomes” the model explains: 0 is as bad as always guessing the average, 1 is a perfect guess
md.m.r2.read: Currently about 0.47–0.58: the position alone explains about half of the result; the rest is later decisions and luck
md.m.ce.meaning: The loss that training actually lowers. The model outputs a value between 0 and 1 (“this seat's final return”); cross-entropy measures its gap to the real result; being confidently wrong is punished especially hard
md.m.note: These two numbers can only be compared on the same validation data. Once the data composition changes they cannot be compared. Always judge a model by its match win rate.
del.title: Delete files
del.blocked: Used by a queued or running job: {files}; cannot be deleted
del.ask: Delete these files? This cannot be undone.
cfg.hint: Tick the boxes on the left to delete configs.
cfg.tracked: {n} of them are built into the repo (tracked by git): after deleting you can restore them with git.
dt.intro: Plays full games with the Runner and samples positions, writing to `results/ml/`. The first time (or after the C# code changed) the Runner is published automatically (needs the .NET 8 SDK).
dt.no_configs: No configs. Add one with “Custom combination”.
dt.custom_hint: Every game is played by the strategies you choose; seat order is reshuffled every game, so every strategy sits in every position. “Add config” only saves the combination as `ml/local/data-configs/<name>.json` (local, not in git; pick it later under “Config”); “Start generating” saves the config and starts.
dt.mcts_slow: MCTS seats are much slower (4 cores, 100 simulations is about 1–2 seconds per game); hand-written strategies and random players play thousands of games per second.
dt.no_model: No {n}-player model yet (it needs a `.meta.json`). Train one from config data first.
dt.sp_sims_help: Self-play trades fewer simulations for more games (v2 used 100)
dt.rate: Sampling rate (chance each decision is sampled)
dt.feature_help: Which feature version describes each position in the data. Defaults to the newest; version 1 is the 430 features used by the old models (v1–v3). Training can only use data of one version, and the trained model belongs to that version.
dt.sp_ref: Reference: 4 cores, 100 simulations, leafRollout 20 is about 1 game/second ({games} games take about {hours} hours).
dt.name: Output name (results/ml/<name>.bin)
dt.p.name: The name cannot be empty or contain path characters or spaces
dt.p.config_taken: A config named {name}.json already exists; choose another name (existing configs are not overwritten)
dt.p.exists: The data already exists (tick to overwrite)
dt.p.pending: A queued or running job already writes this file name; choose another name
dt.twins: Data with the same recipe (same config, seed, games and sampling rate) already exists: {list}. Running again gives the same content, so it is usually not needed.
dt.save_note: Only saved as ml/local/data-configs/{name}.json; no data is generated
dt.saved: Saved ml/local/data-configs/{name}.json: you can pick it under “Config” later.
dt.delete_hint: Tick the boxes on the left to delete data (with its .json); to choose what to train on, go to the “{page}” page.
job.started_queued: Added to the queue (No. {pos}); it starts automatically when the jobs ahead finish.
job.started_now: Job started: progress is at the bottom of the left navigation and on the “{page}” page.
